items.label: MEC press release: Notice Regarding Additional Capital Investment (Acquisition (09-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: MEC decided on additional capital investment of approx. JPY

set.signal: MEC decided on additional capital investment of approx. JPY 2 billion - the second phase of construction of its new Kitakyushu Factory, which is scheduled to begin operations in December 2026 - to strengthen facilities that will produce chemical products for semiconductor package substrates, with start of operation planned for FY2028. The company had planned to raise the new factory's capacity as needed, but says that against the backdrop of increased AI-related investment, demand for products related to semiconductor package substrates is expected to greatly increase, particularly for the company, so it is investing beyond the scope of the original plan; the investment also aims to strengthen its business continuity plan by decentralizing production bases. Impact on results for the fiscal year ending December 2026 is described as immaterial.

items.label: MEC press release: Notice Regarding Acquisition of Noncurrent Assets (09-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: MEC's board resolved to acquire land and buildings adjacent

set.signal: MEC's board resolved to acquire land and buildings adjacent to its Nagaoka Factory (Nagaoka City, Niigata Prefecture), its mass-production factory in Japan, for approx. JPY 2.3 billion; contract dated September 30, 2026, property handover March 31, 2027. The company says the Nagaoka Factory will mark 40 years of operation in 2033 and is expected to undergo major upgrades, and the land expands its options for renovating the factory, as part of strengthening its group-wide supply structure for expanding AI-driven demand for electronic substrates and components. MEC states it has a particularly high market share in chemicals for the package-substrate manufacturing process. Impact on results for the fiscal year ending December 2026 is described as immaterial.
